observation.visible_scene: A close, mostly top-down view of a shallow water surface lying over a dark brownish substrate, entirely covered by a web-like network of bright yellowish-white sunlight caustics. In many frames a small cluster of dark plant-like shapes or debris is visible hanging at the top edge of the frame.
visible_changes: The caustic network continuously morphs: the bright lines bend, stretch, merge and split, and the luminous nodes where lines intersect drift across the frame, consistent with a rippling water surface rather than a static pattern.
Bright patches within the network expand and contract and shift position from frame to frame, while the overall layout of dark cells enclosed by bright lines is retained throughout the excerpt.
The dark plant-like shapes at the top edge change their horizontal position and partly move out of and back into view over the course of the clip.
No separate solid object, animal, or person enters or leaves the water; the only visible motion is the deformation/translation of the light pattern and the slight movement of the top-edge vegetation.
outside_clip_unknowns: What is producing the water motion (wind, current, an unseen disturbance) is not shown.
The full shape and extent of the vegetation above the top edge, and whether the camera is fixed or handheld, are not determined within this segment.
Whether the excerpt begins or ends mid-ripple is unknown; both ends are arbitrary crop boundaries.
uncertain_details: The small apparent drift of the whole frame and of the top-edge vegetation cannot be cleanly attributed to camera movement versus movement of the water/vegetation, so camera motion is treated as uncertain.
Individual caustic lines cannot be reliably tracked as the same physical feature from one frame to the next due to the rapid, non-rigid deformation.
